skill.name: omakase-off
skill.description: Guides software build requests through brainstorming, optional parallel approach exploration, variant implementation, scenario testing, and winner selection.
skill.summary: Explore competing software implementation approaches in parallel and choose a tested winner.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and ordinary planning language. No prompt injection or network reconnaissance evidence was found. One medium semantic risk remains because the workflow directs deletion of losing worktrees and branches during cleanup.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, dirty-state checks, and recovery guidance before removing worktrees or deleting branches.
Document that the workflow may create and delete branches and worktrees, and recommend use only in user-owned repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Git Cleanup Without Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow instructs cleanup of losing variants with git worktree removal and branch deletion. Without an explicit confirmation and dirty-state check, this could delete useful local work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly require cleanup of loser worktrees and show branch deletion commands. The risk is contextual because cleanup can be safe when confirmed and checked first.

content.value_statement: Software build requests often have unclear architectural choices. This skill guides brainstorming, parallel implementation, testing, and winner selection.
actual_capabilities: Presents a brainstorm or omakase choice before detailed build planning.
Detects repeated uncertainty about architectural decisions during brainstorming.
Defines variant plans under a shared feature planning directory.
Orchestrates parallel agent implementation using isolated worktrees.
Requires scenario testing, fresh review, and judging before completion.
Documents the winning approach and cleanup results.
limitations: Depends on referenced skills or fallback workflows for full execution.
Can create several branches and worktrees in one repository.
Needs user context before it can choose useful implementation variants.
Cleanup steps require care to avoid deleting useful local work.

use_cases.title: Choose a Feature Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare storage, API, or framework options by implementing focused variants and testing them against the same scenarios.

use_cases.title: Resolve Product Ambiguity
use_cases.description: Turn uncertain requirements into a small set of concrete implementation paths for stakeholder review.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Technical Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Use real code, tests, and reviews to compare maintainability, fit, and implementation cost.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a simple feature request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a small CLI todo app. Use omakase-off to help me choose the best approach.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.scenario: You already know the main alternatives.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement this feature with two variants: one using JSON storage and one using SQLite. Compare them with scenario tests.

prompt_templates.title: Find Open Decisions
prompt_templates.scenario: You want help identifying architectural choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Brainstorm this dashboard feature with me. If I seem undecided about architecture, offer parallel exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Omakase Evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use the complete workflow for a high-impact feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use omakase-off for this authentication redesign. Generate variants, plan each one, test them equally, review survivors, and recommend a winner.

output_examples.input: Build a todo CLI, but I am unsure whether storage should be JSON or SQLite.
output_examples.output: The skill captures storage as an architectural slot, creates two variants, tests both with the same scenarios, and reports a winner.

output_examples.input: Add authentication to my app. I do not know whether sessions or tokens fit better.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes session and token variants, plans each path, compares scenario results, and highlights tradeoffs for selection.

output_examples.input: Create a data import feature and pick the best implementation path.
output_examples.output: The skill gathers essential context, generates distinct implementation approaches, runs reviews, and documents why the selected approach won.

best_practices: Use omakase when architectural choices affect maintainability, performance, or user workflow.
Keep variant count capped and define the primary decision axis first.
Review scenario results before selecting or merging a winning variant.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow for trivial naming or file placement decisions.
Running cleanup before checking branches for uncommitted or useful work.
Comparing variants with different tests or acceptance criteria.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps explore multiple implementation approaches in parallel, then compares them with tests and review.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a build request has important architectural choices and no obvious best path.

faq.question: Does it replace brainstorming?
faq.answer: No. It can start with brainstorming, then offer parallel exploration when important uncertainty appears.

faq.question: How many variants does it create?
faq.answer: The workflow caps exploration at about five or six variants to avoid unnecessary work.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: It references planning, worktree, testing, review, and finishing skills, with fallback behavior when they are unavailable.

faq.question: What should users review before cleanup?
faq.answer: Users should check dirty worktrees, unmerged commits, and branch value before deleting losing variants.
